headline: The RBA held rates but warned more hikes aren't off the table — while a US-Iran peace deal sent oil crashing 5.6% and gave TTWO a big 6.2% lift on GTA 6 hype.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO surged 6.2% last night on a wave of GTA 6 excitement — gamers are marking June 23 on their calendars for what's expected to be a major reveal or release milestone. Analysts are also pointing out that GTA 6 is a massive accelerant for the business, not just a one-off event. The stock is still slightly underwater overall on your position, but the momentum is real.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS dropped 4.5% today, giving back recent gains. Oil's big fall (tied to a US-Iran peace deal easing geopolitical risk) dragged on commodities broadly, and lithium stocks tend to get caught in that net. There's some positive noise around spodumene prices tightening and solid-state battery demand long-term, but near-term sentiment is shaky.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: Oil (WTI crude) crashed 5.6% last night after a US-Iran breakthrough deal was announced, slashing geopolitical risk. Major banks including Goldman Sachs have already cut their oil price forecasts in response. As an energy sector ETF, FUEL directly tracks these global energy companies — when oil falls this hard, the whole sector follows.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft slipped 1.4% last night, underperforming the broader market. There's no single big catalyst — it looks like general rotation and profit-taking in large-cap tech. MSFT remains your biggest underwater position, down about $44 AUD overall.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI nudged up 1.2% today, riding positive sentiment around AI stocks. Some analysts are pointing out that the US-Iran deal removed a key macro risk (higher oil = higher costs for data centres), which is a mild tailwind for AI infrastructure plays.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google ticked up 1.1% last night in a relatively quiet session. No major news catalyst — it's been a steady mover lately. Your position is up a healthy 28.4% overall.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS edged up 0.5% today on the ASX, tracking the prior US session's mixed performance. The US market pulled back last night (S&P -0.5%, NASDAQ -1.1%), but the ASX-listed ETF's pricing reflects a slight lag and currency movements.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE gained a modest 0.4% today. Emerging markets have been relatively calm, and the AUD holding steady near 70.7 US cents isn't hurting returns from this one.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG was essentially flat today, up just 3 cents. As a diversified fund holding a mix of Aussie and international shares, it tends to smooth out the daily noise — which is exactly what it's doing here.

watch_today.title: RBA holds rates — but warns hikes aren't done
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank kept the official cash rate at 4.35% today but explicitly refused to rule out future rises, saying nine words no borrower wanted to hear. If you're tracking mortgage costs or property-sensitive stocks, this is a 'watch this week' situation — the hawkish (rate-hike-leaning) tone could weigh on consumer confidence and rate-sensitive sectors.

watch_today.title: Oil crashed 5.6% — FUEL.AX is hurting
watch_today.detail: WTI crude fell from $80.75 to $76.25 a barrel last night after the US and Iran struck a peace deal, removing a big chunk of Middle East tension that had been propping up prices. Goldman Sachs and others have already cut oil price targets. Your FUEL.AX position is down 2.1% today and at risk of more near-term pressure if oil keeps falling. Consider whether you want to hold through what could be a prolonged price reset.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 buzz hitting hard — June 23 in the calendar
watch_today.detail: Take-Two Interactive jumped 6.2% last night as GTA 6 hype builds toward what gamers are circling as a key June 23 date. Analysts at Insider Monkey note GTA 6 is an accelerant for TTWO's whole business, not just a single game launch. Your position is still marginally underwater overall (-$4.59 AUD), but this momentum is worth watching. No reason to sell into strength — hold and see what the June 23 reveal brings.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Sharp 4.5% drop today — lithium under pressure
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals fell hard today, caught in a broader commodity selloff tied to easing geopolitical risk and oil's big drop. Your position is already down 8.2% overall (-$12.24 AUD). The long-term lithium story (solid-state batteries, EV demand) is intact, but near-term sentiment is weak. Hold for now unless your conviction on the long-term thesis has changed.

watch_today.title: MSFT continues to underperform — keep an eye on it
watch_today.detail: Microsoft fell another 1.4% last night and remains your biggest dollar loss at -$43.83 AUD. There's no single news catalyst — it's just not getting the same AI excitement bump as Google right now. Nothing screams 'sell', but if you're looking to rebalance, MSFT is the position most worth reviewing.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: AI ETF catching a tailwind
watch_today.detail: Your Global X AI ETF gained 1.2% today and analysts are pointing to the US-Iran deal as a mild positive — cheaper oil means lower energy costs for AI data centres. The long-term AI infrastructure buildout story is still very much intact. Hold and let it run.

markets.summary: Last night on Wall Street, both major indices retreated — the S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the NASDAQ dropped 1.1%, weighed down by tech weakness (MSFT dragged). The big macro story was oil crashing 5.6% after a US-Iran peace deal, which eased geopolitical risk but hurt energy stocks. Gold ticked higher to $4,359 USD an ounce — investors still want some safe-haven protection. The Aussie dollar was almost unchanged at 70.7 US cents. The ASX 200's closing data wasn't available at time of writing.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is the RBA keeping rates on hold at 4.35% but refusing to rule out future hikes — a sting in the tail for borrowers. There's also movement on CGT (capital gains tax) reform, with the government reportedly looking at fast-tracking some carve-outs after growing criticism.

stories.title: RBA holds cash rate at 4.35% but won't rule out future hikes
stories.source: Reserve Bank of Australia / The Guardian
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank kept the official cash rate at 4.35% at today's meeting — no change, so no relief for mortgage holders just yet. But the board refused to rule out future rate increases, which is the hawkish (leaning toward raising rates) signal that spooked markets. The nine words getting attention: the RBA said it was 'not ruling out' further rate hikes if inflation stays stubborn. For anyone with a variable-rate mortgage or exposure to consumer-facing stocks, this is a reminder that the rate pain may not be over.

stories.title: 'Not ruling out': RBA warns rate pain not over
stories.why_it_matters: Despite holding steady today, the RBA's statement has a clear warning embedded in it: if inflation doesn't keep coming down, another rate rise is on the cards. This comes on top of the May rate hold, meaning the RBA is firmly in 'wait and see' mode — but the door to further hikes is deliberately being left open. Economists will be closely watching the next inflation print as the key trigger.

stories.title: Government might fast-track CGT carve-outs as criticism grows
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government is reportedly considering fast-tracking carve-outs to its proposed CGT (capital gains tax — the tax you pay when you sell an asset for a profit) reforms, after a backlash grew louder. The original proposal would have raised the effective tax on investment gains. If carve-outs are introduced quickly, some investors — particularly those holding property or shares in their own name — may be less affected than initially feared. Details are still emerging.

ai.summary: Today's AI news is dominated by regulation — the US has curbed Anthropic's exports, the EU is moving to ban AI nudifiers, and there's a broader debate about whether smart regulation could actually give Western AI companies a competitive edge. Nothing that directly moves your GXAI.AX today, but the regulatory backdrop is getting more complex.

stories.title: US curbs Anthropic AI exports — sector rattled
stories.why_it_matters: The US government has imposed restrictions on Anthropic (the company behind the Claude AI models) around international exports of its technology. This is part of a growing trend of treating advanced AI as a strategic national asset, similar to how semiconductors are controlled. For investors in AI ETFs like GXAI.AX, it's a reminder that regulatory risk — not just competition — is a real factor. It could also advantage US-based AI incumbents like Google if rivals face restrictions.

stories.title: EU lawmakers move to ban AI nudifiers — enforcement still unclear
stories.why_it_matters: European lawmakers are pushing to ban AI tools that generate non-consensual intimate images (so-called 'nudifiers'). The ban is part of a broader EU push to regulate harmful AI applications. The catch: enforcement is still murky, as these tools are often hosted outside EU borders. It signals Europe is getting more aggressive about AI harms, which could mean compliance costs for any AI company wanting to operate there.

stories.title: How regulation could be America's competitive AI advantage
stories.why_it_matters: An interesting counterintuitive argument gaining traction: smart, targeted AI regulation in the US could actually cement American companies' lead, by setting global standards that others have to follow. The logic is that whoever writes the rulebook shapes the playing field — and US companies like Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic are already building to those standards. Worth watching as the regulatory debate heats up globally.

stories.title: Frontier AI lab landscape: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta — who's winning?
stories.why_it_matters: A business-focused breakdown of where the four main AI labs — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and Meta AI — sit competitively right now. Google continues to be a strong contender with Gemini, which is directly relevant to your GOOG holding. The key takeaway is that the AI race is a multi-horse contest, and no single company has locked up the market. Diversified exposure (like GXAI.AX) makes sense in this environment.

sport.summary: NRL Round 16 kicks off Friday with the Gold Coast Titans hosting Penrith at Cbus Super Stadium on Saturday arvo. AFL has a few talking points today — a major review announced by the AFL, and SA locking in the Gather Round through to 2029. The Williams sisters are also making tennis news ahead of Wimbledon.

stories.title: NRL Round 16 team lists confirmed — Titans host Panthers on Saturday
stories.why_it_matters: Round 16 team lists are out. Your local team the Titans host the Panthers at Cbus Super Stadium this Saturday at 5:30pm — always a big one given Penrith's recent dynasty. The full draw also includes Knights vs Dragons (Fri), Tigers vs Dolphins (Sat), Bulldogs vs Sea Eagles (Sat), and a Sunday triple-header of Warriors/Cowboys, Storm/Raiders, and Roosters/Sharks. Broncos, Eels, and Rabbitohs are all on the bye.

stories.title: AFL announces major review by the board
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL board has announced a major review today, though the scope and specific focus areas aren't fully detailed in available reporting. It comes amid broader discussion about the competition's direction and clubs making 'big picture' decisions rather than just chasing wins. Worth keeping an eye on as details emerge.

stories.title: South Australia locks in AFL Gather Round until 2029
stories.why_it_matters: South Australia has secured an extension of the AFL Gather Round — the league's festival-of-football weekend held in Adelaide — through to 2029. It's a significant economic win for SA, with the event drawing fans and tourism dollars from across the country. Good news for Adelaide's economy and a sign the AFL is doubling down on the concept after its early success.

stories.title: Williams sisters team up for doubles after 10 years apart
stories.why_it_matters: Venus and Serena Williams are reportedly teaming up for doubles for the first time in 10 years, chasing a shot at Wimbledon. The Williams sisters last played doubles together in 2016, so this is a major tennis moment. No confirmation yet on the exact tournament, but the buzz around a potential Wimbledon run is building.
